test: Position-report cadence DURING motion -- the measurement the direction review needed
why_this_run_existed: The 2026-08-06 direction review asserted a 1.11 s position update interval; that figure was the sampler's own rate and was withdrawn. The 2026-08-07 per-channel probe then showed the position channel is silent while the mower is stationary, so the cadence could only be measured with the mower moving.

method.sampler: export_runtime_state polled externally, median 89 ms interval = 11.2 Hz
method.oversampling: ~12x the cadence being resolved, so the 2026-08-06 confound cannot recur
method.why_this_works: coordinator.data is mutated in place by pymammotion as reports arrive, so a fast external poll observes real arrivals rather than a coordinator tick

conditions.rtk: Fix throughout the entire run -- no drop to Float under motion

RESULT_position_update_interval_ms.note: The long tail is the stationary intervals between pulses, when the channel goes silent as established earlier the same day. The moving cadence is the min/p10/median cluster: roughly one update per second.

RESULT_distance_per_update_while_moving.note: MEASURED, not inferred from an assumed rate. This is how far the mower travels between successive position reports at the fast tier's operating speed.

what_this_establishes.headline: The position feed updates about once per second during motion, and at the fast tier the mower covers ~47 cm between updates.
what_this_establishes.consequence_for_tolerance: A stop decision is made against a position that can be up to ~47 cm stale. An 0.08 m waypoint tolerance is therefore NOT achievable at the fast tier by any control law -- the information required arrives less often than the error accumulates. This restores the direction review's conclusion, but now on a sound 12x-oversampled measurement rather than the withdrawn one.
what_this_establishes.speed_required_for_8cm: 0.08 m / 1.03 s = about 0.078 m/s. The existing slow tier measures ~0.10 m/s, giving ~10 cm per update -- still marginally too fast.
what_this_establishes.speed_supported_by_current_slow_tier: ~0.10 m/s x 1.03 s = ~10-11 cm per update, which is consistent with a 0.15 m tolerance and not with 0.08 m.

secondary_findings.rtk_held_fix_under_motion: RTK read Fix across all 1627 samples. The base-station power cycle earlier that evening held up under driving -- this was an open risk and is now closed.
secondary_findings.clean_run: stop_reason target_reached, 5 commands (1 turn + 3 linear), pulses 0.4754 / 0.5811 / 0.3943 m = 1.451 m for a 1.5 m leg. One turn command only. No reverse-recovery guard trigger. This is the first clean, well-tracked pass of the session and it happened under RTK Fix -- a contrast with the Float-era overshoot runs worth noting but NOT worth over-reading from one run.

caveats: One run, one mower, one speed tier. The slow tier's cadence was not separately measured.
The median is dominated by the fast tier; whether the device reports faster at lower speeds is unknown.
Distance-per-update depends on speed, so the 47 cm figure is specific to the fast tier.
No gate is claimed. target_reached here was a 1.5 m single segment at a deliberately loosened 0.15 m tolerance, not a Gate 4 geometry.
